source.rule: A fixed top-level system prelife age advances the first calendar PM to the next 100-hour multiple. AGE 120 therefore leaves 80 hours. The CLI Prelife Log is enabled transiently and the prior user option restored after each run.

hypothesis_before_native.zero-age: All three aircraft have zero initial calendar age; their first CAL100 PMs start at h100.
hypothesis_before_native.fixed-ages: The Prelife Log reports one aircraft each at CALHOURS ages 0, 60 and 120. Their first CAL100 PMs start at h100, h40 and h80 respectively. The age-120 aircraft rolls to the next 100-hour cycle, leaving 80 hours.

predeclared_native_acceptance: Both arms import/export authored populated tables exactly, convert with zero errors, calculate with no unreviewed runtime errors, preserve the existing GUI process and native queue, and seal complete source/raw evidence hashes.
The arms differ only in Prelife, PrelifeData, SystemDeployment.PLID and descriptive text; aircraft count, PM, schedule, seed and horizon are identical.

The native _Prelife.log shows per-entity CALHOURS ages and PLINDs for the fixed arm; model event log maps the same entity IDs to first CAL100 PM starts at h40, h80 and h100. The zero-age arm first PMs start at h100. The registry Prelife Log setting is restored to NO after each run.
A separate reviewer independently replays frozen source and raw evidence without importing author validation code.
limits: Three same-type aircraft, fixed top-level system calendar ages, one seed and one 100-hour PM only.
No installed item, stocked item, other prelife pattern or other operation parameter in this variant.
Age interpretation is checked by the Prelife Log and the first PM event; no claim about later PM cycles or stochastic outcomes.
